newsitem.title: GUAM: Guam governor hero in KAL crash rescue.
newsitem.headline: Guam governor hero in KAL crash rescue.

text.p: Guam governor Carl Gutierrez on Thursday emerged as the hero of the Korean Air Lines (KAL) plane crash, appearing with the little Japanese girl he saved from the burning wreckage.
Gutierrez, one of the first to arrive at the crash site in the early hours of Wednesday, pulled 11-year old Rika Matsuda to safety.
"You don't stop to think in a case like that," he told a news conference at his official Guam residence, at which Rika and her father appeared with him.
Rika, clutching a toy animal as she sat between the governor and her father, looked well, although she had some scars on the right side of her face.
Gutierrez said he shook Rika to revive her and after she came to, she clung to him for some time.
Gutierrez and his small team of rescuers pulled several others from the wrecked Boeing 747, which went down with 254 people aboard.
Rika escaped the disaster with minor cuts and bruises and concussions and was recovering quickly, her father Tatsuo said.

"I thank the governor, the rescue workers, the hospital officials and the people of Guam," the father, who had flown in from Japan, told the news conference. "Thanks to all of you, it seems Rika is all right now."
Rika's mother was believed to have perished in the flames which engulfed the plane.
"It didn't look good," Gutierrez said in reply to a question if he thought there was a chance that Rika's mother survived.
During her rescue, Rika repeatedly pointed in the direction where she thought her mother was, Gutierrez said.
The 747, on a flight from Seoul to Guam, crashed only three miles (five km) from the airport runway as it made its landing approach in a heavy downpour.
About 30 people were rescued and taken to Guam hospitals but as of late Thursday, only 27, including Rika, were still alive.
Some of the survivors were severely burned and were to be evacuated to South Korea on a U.S. military hospital plane, local radio stations said.

Rika said nothing during the news conference but was quoted as saying during an earlier interview that her only ailment was that her back hurt because she had been forced to stay in a hospital bed for too long.
